doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: The Indiana Brass Band and parades for funerals
summary: Puzzling over the name of the Indiana Brass Band, which George joined as the youngest around 1905; bands played big parades and funerals.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You know, they played trumpet when they had the, uh, what you call them? You don't know about it. The Indiana Brass Band. You remember?
Why did they call that the Indiana Band?
I don't know why they gave it that name, but as I tell you, my husband was the youngest in there. He was the only young fellow Indian there on the Brass Band. All of them was old men.
Well, you see, a long time ago, I'd like to play like Maple Leafs. They'll name a band something, something nice flower. Yeah. Yeah. So, maybe we thought about Indiana.
I don't know why they named it,

and I'm not asking why. Maybe we was playing back home in Indiana. But I do remember, anything. How old would you be? How old would you be? How old would you be? I don't know if you were in the youngest man. How old would you be?
Well, I see. My children would have a bone. I mean, how old would you be? That would be a good way of finding out.
That Indiana Band, was that when you were first married?

Yeah, when I was first married. When I was first married. About 19... About 1905. About 1905. But they established that during that time. You see? It was third on them. And then afterwards, they still helped up the Indiana Grass Band.
Did they play like the Grass Band students that are released for fume roles?
For fume. That's all they played for. Big parades and fume roles.
Fumes, yeah. Then they hired a band, you know, for fume, but now they don't. Some fumes had two and three bands.
Did you know that? Yeah. Two and three bands on one fume. We had five on Old Man Island. Yeah. They wanted to.
